concepts.name: Carbon bonding and hybridisation
concepts.summary: Explain how carbon forms four bonds and how sp3, sp2 and sp hybridisation determine geometry.

concepts.name: Structural representations
concepts.summary: Read and draw Lewis, condensed and skeletal structures and interpret implied carbons and hydrogens.

concepts.name: Common functional groups
concepts.summary: Recognise alcohols, ethers, amines, aldehydes, ketones, carboxylic acids, esters, amides and alkenes/alkynes in structures.

concepts.name: IUPAC alkane nomenclature
concepts.summary: Name branched alkanes and simple substituted compounds by finding the parent chain and numbering substituents.

concepts.name: Isomerism types
concepts.summary: Distinguish constitutional isomers from stereoisomers and draw isomers of a given formula.

concepts.name: Polarity and intermolecular forces
concepts.summary: Relate bond polarity and intermolecular forces to boiling point and solubility of organic compounds.

misconceptions.text: Each vertex and line end in a skeletal structure is a carbon with no hydrogens attached.
Molecules with the same molecular formula are the same compound.
Larger molecules always have higher boiling points regardless of functional groups or branching.

concepts.name: Conformations of alkanes and cyclohexane
concepts.summary: Draw Newman projections and chair cyclohexanes and identify axial and equatorial positions and the more stable conformer.

concepts.name: Chirality and R/S assignment
concepts.summary: Identify stereocentres and assign R/S configuration using Cahn-Ingold-Prelog priorities.

concepts.name: Enantiomers, diastereomers and meso compounds
concepts.summary: Classify pairs of stereoisomers and recognise meso compounds from their symmetry.

concepts.name: Acid-base reactions of organic compounds
concepts.summary: Use pKa values and structural effects to predict acid strength and the direction of proton transfer.

concepts.name: Curved-arrow notation
concepts.summary: Draw curved arrows showing electron-pair movement for simple steps and resonance structures.

concepts.name: Nucleophiles, electrophiles and leaving groups
concepts.summary: Identify nucleophilic and electrophilic sites and judge what makes a good leaving group.

concepts.name: Alkene addition reactions
concepts.summary: Predict products of HX addition, hydration and halogenation of alkenes using Markovnikov's rule.

misconceptions.text: R and S configuration tells you whether a compound rotates light clockwise or counterclockwise.
Any molecule with a stereocentre is chiral.
In a chair cyclohexane, substituents prefer the axial position.

concepts.name: SN2 and SN1 mechanisms
concepts.summary: Analyse substrate, nucleophile, leaving group and solvent to decide between SN1 and SN2 and predict stereochemical outcome.

concepts.name: Carbocation stability and rearrangements
concepts.summary: Rank carbocation stability and recognise when shifts give more stable intermediates.

concepts.name: E1 and E2 eliminations
concepts.summary: Predict elimination products and regiochemistry and distinguish elimination from substitution competition.

concepts.name: Alcohol and ether reactions
concepts.summary: Predict outcomes of alcohol oxidation, conversion to halides and sulfonates, and ether cleavage and epoxide opening.

concepts.name: Carbonyl nucleophilic addition
concepts.summary: Explain and predict additions of Grignard reagents, hydrides and cyanide to aldehydes and ketones.

concepts.name: Spectroscopic structure determination
concepts.summary: Combine IR, 1H and 13C NMR and mass spectra to deduce the structure of an unknown.

concepts.name: Aromaticity and electrophilic substitution
concepts.summary: Apply Hückel's rule and analyse how substituents direct electrophilic aromatic substitution.

misconceptions.text: SN2 reactions proceed with retention of configuration, or racemise the stereocentre.
Substitution and elimination are separate reactions that never compete.
All substituents on a benzene ring direct incoming electrophiles to the ortho and para positions.

concepts.name: Enolate chemistry
concepts.summary: Analyse enolate formation and its use in alkylation, aldol and Claisen reactions including kinetic versus thermodynamic control.

concepts.name: Carboxylic acid derivative interconversion
concepts.summary: Use relative reactivity to predict nucleophilic acyl substitution among acid chlorides, anhydrides, esters and amides.

concepts.name: Retrosynthetic analysis
concepts.summary: Work backward from a target by disconnections and evaluate alternative routes.

concepts.name: Chemoselectivity and protecting groups
concepts.summary: Judge when protecting groups are needed and choose ones compatible with the reaction conditions.

concepts.name: Pericyclic reactions
concepts.summary: Predict Diels-Alder outcomes including regiochemistry and endo stereochemistry using orbital symmetry ideas.

concepts.name: Conjugate addition and amine chemistry
concepts.summary: Distinguish 1,2- from 1,4-addition and design routes to amines via reductive amination and related methods.

concepts.name: Stereochemical control in reactions
concepts.summary: Evaluate stereospecific and stereoselective reactions and predict the stereochemistry of products.

misconceptions.text: A synthesis route is good if each step works in isolation, regardless of other functional groups present.
Aldol reactions always give a single product regardless of which carbonyl compounds are mixed.
Any carboxylic acid derivative can be converted into any other by simple nucleophile addition.

concepts.name: Frontier orbital and physical organic analysis
concepts.summary: Use orbital theory, kinetics, linear free-energy relationships and isotope effects to evaluate proposed mechanisms.

concepts.name: Transition metal cross-coupling
concepts.summary: Evaluate palladium-catalysed coupling mechanisms and choose coupling strategies for carbon-carbon bond construction.

concepts.name: Radical and photochemical reactions
concepts.summary: Evaluate radical chain processes and photochemical pathways and their selectivity relative to polar chemistry.

concepts.name: Conformational and stereoelectronic control
concepts.summary: Assess how conformation and orbital alignment dictate diastereoselectivity and reactivity in acyclic and cyclic systems.

concepts.name: Asymmetric synthesis strategies
concepts.summary: Design enantioselective routes using chiral pool, auxiliaries or catalysts and justify the choice.

concepts.name: Multistep total synthesis planning
concepts.summary: Devise efficient convergent syntheses for complex molecules balancing step count, selectivity and protecting-group economy.

misconceptions.text: A reaction that gives the expected product proves the proposed mechanism is correct.
Cross-coupling works equally well with any halide, organometallic partner and ligand.
Enantioselective catalysis simply makes only the favoured product by blocking the other enantiomer entirely.
